gaps.sentence: My brother is six foot three — he is much ___ than me.
gaps.explanation: 'Tall' is used for people's height, so the comparative is 'taller'; 'higher' is for heights above a level.

gaps.sentence: The Sahara is the largest hot ___ in the world.
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is a dry region with little rain; 'dessert' is the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

gaps.sentence: The two leaders signed a ___ peace agreement.
gaps.hint: important enough to be remembered in history
gaps.explanation: 'Historic' means important or famous in history; 'historical' just means connected with the past or the study of history.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ anything left in the fridge.
gaps.hint: adverb meaning almost not at all
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly' means almost not ('hardly anything'); 'hard' means with effort or solid.
